progressiveDisclosure.note: Below this skill count, walk the branches directly. Above it, add a two-stage walk: a cheap pass over catalog summaries, then a rerank of the top few with full text. The catalog summary field exists to keep this open.

agent-delegation.routeWhen: Use when the orchestrator composes or dispatches a worker package, picks a role, verifies evidence, or consolidates escalations.

architecture-and-skeleton.routeWhen: Use when choosing a stack or architecture, when how to structure this comes up, or before any real feature is built.

avo.routeWhen: Use when building, extending, or reviewing Avo resources, fields, actions, dashboards, cards, or authorization in the user's Rails modules or applications.

beeper-bridge.routeWhen: Use when the user attaches, detaches, or checks the Beeper↔opencode bridge — including 'establish a bridge connection to Beeper', 'I'm going AFK', or 'delegate this to Beeper'.

code-review.routeWhen: Use when reviewing a pull request or change, or when preparing a change for review.

communication-standards.routeWhen: Use for all user-facing writing — conversation, summaries, plans, reviews, and teaching — or when the user asks for less AI slop, a different tone, or a style guide.

customize-opencode.routeWhen: Use when the user is editing or creating opencode's own configuration — opencode.json, .opencode/, or ~/.config/opencode/ — including agents, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers, and permission rules.

discovery-interview.routeWhen: Use when a brief is vague, when starting discovery, or when the user hands over raw material and asks to figure out what we're building.

docker.routeWhen: Use when creating or changing a Docker or Docker Compose dev environment — adding a service to docker-base, extending a language wrapper, wiring a project's compose, or defining the production image.

edge-case-analysis.routeWhen: Use when reviewing code for edge cases, crashes, hangs, and denial-of-service, or as the robustness step of a red-team review.

feature-spec.routeWhen: Use when writing or updating a feature spec, or when a slice needs its acceptance criteria pinned.

filament.routeWhen: Use when building, extending, or reviewing Filament resources, forms, tables, plugins, or pages in the user's Laravel modules or applications.

git-workflow.routeWhen: Use when the user asks to commit, branch, merge, rebase, stash, push, pull, open or review a pull request, file or triage an issue, create a release, author a CONTRIBUTING.md, or when starting work in a repo and the workflow needs to be determined.

github.routeWhen: Use when reading or triaging GitHub issues, joining or posting in discussions, sending updates, or creating pull requests that reference issues.

jev-gates.routeWhen: Use when the orchestrator needs a single classification call — a triage decision, routing a task to a skill, matrix row, or worker role, pre-screening a worker diff, or deciding whether to escalate to the advisor.

kubernetes.routeWhen: Use when deploying to Kubernetes, writing or changing a Helm chart, wiring Flux, handling cluster secrets, or working with k3s, cert-manager, GHCR, or the kubernetes-* repos.

laravel.routeWhen: Use when building, extending, or reviewing Laravel or PHP code in the user's style, or when the task references their modules, ServiceProvider, composer wiring, or Eloquent mechanics.

memory.routeWhen: Use when reading or writing HOT.md, recording episodic events, updating semantic memory, running reflection, or when the user says consolidate memory.

new-project.routeWhen: Use when starting a new project from scratch, scaffolding a new repo, creating a new Laravel app or module, or setting up a fresh development environment.

obsidian-plugin.routeWhen: Use when building, extending, or releasing an Obsidian community plugin in any repository.

premise-demolition.routeWhen: Use when scrutinising an existing system or a module's architecture against its spec with fresh eyes, when a design feels over-engineered, or before any re-architecture, at system scale.

project-seed.routeWhen: Use when starting a new project, setting up the foundation, or seeding a repo for spec-driven delivery.

rails.routeWhen: Use when building, extending, or reviewing Ruby on Rails code, engines, modules, action objects, DTOs, ActiveRecord models, Hotwire views, or Packwerk boundaries in the user's repos.

refactoring.routeWhen: Use when a change's main job is a behaviour-preserving restructure of code, at any scale, including when deciding how much machinery the refactor deserves.

research-prompt-skills.routeWhen: Use when running the research-prompt-skills scheduled job or when asked to do a prompt, memory, context, or skill research sweep.

security-review.routeWhen: Use when reviewing a diff or codebase for security issues, or as the core red-team step of a code review.

self-documenting-code.routeWhen: Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code, when deciding whether a comment earns its place, or for any question of code style, formatting rhythm, blank lines, or error-message wording.

shape-up.routeWhen: Use when shaping a piece of work, setting an appetite, betting on a cycle, tracking a hill, or sizing a slice.

skeleton-ecosystem.routeWhen: Use when scaffolding or adopting a repo, choosing a skeleton, or wiring a devshell, workflows or shared config.

skill-authoring.routeWhen: Use when creating a new SKILL.md, editing or extending an existing skill, or formalizing a workflow as a reusable agent skill per the Agent Skills specification.

skill-design-principles.routeWhen: Use before authoring a skill when deciding whether a skill is needed, what belongs in it, or whether the thing is a skill or a role.

slice-delivery.routeWhen: Use when starting or delivering a slice, or when the user asks to build the next slice.

software-architecture.routeWhen: Use when designing, building, extending, or reviewing the architecture of any OO codebase, or when deciding where logic lives, how a use case is shaped, or how a port or DTO is defined.

software-architecture-structure.routeWhen: Use when creating, moving, naming, or placing a class or file, choosing a folder, picking a role suffix, adding a module, or reviewing a repository's structure.

software-development.routeWhen: Use when building, extending, refactoring, or reviewing code in any language or repository, or when deciding how to structure a change.

software-testing.routeWhen: Use when writing, extending, or reviewing tests, or when deciding what to test and how to structure a test suite.

spec-change.routeWhen: Use when the user changes their mind mid-build, when a requirement shifts, or when implementation surfaces an ambiguity the spec does not cover.

systemd-scheduler.routeWhen: Use when scheduling a recurring agent job, adding, removing, or changing a scheduled job, or inspecting why a scheduled run behaved a certain way.

systems-thinking.routeWhen: Use when modelling a system or feature for the first time, when asked whether a design is right, or as the first move of a re-architecture.

teach-mode.routeWhen: Use when the user wants to learn a subject — 'teach me X', 'walk me through X', 'give me a lesson on X', or 'explain X to me' with a learning intent.

threat-modeling.routeWhen: Use when reviewing architecture or design for security, scoping a security review, or as the first step of a red-team or adversarial review.

typescript.routeWhen: Use when writing, extending, or reviewing TypeScript or Node code, naming an interface or type, deciding a module's export shape, wiring dependencies, or configuring tsconfig.

typst-document.routeWhen: Use when converting a markdown document to a PDF, creating an offerte or contract, or rendering a document with the 99linesofcode typst template.

vault-notes.routeWhen: Use when creating or maintaining a note, person, organization, project, or meeting in the Obsidian vault, or when reorganizing or cleaning the vault.

wiki.routeWhen: Use when ingesting a source from the vault Inbox, querying the wiki, or linting wiki health.
